content:
{
  "findings": [
    {
      "title": "Primary endpoint analysis not specified",
      "quote": "the analysis of the primary efficacy endpoint of PFS will only be reported in a descriptive manner.",
      "page": 81,
      "section": "9.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "critical",
      "explanation": "The protocol states that PFS will be reported descriptively but does not specify the exact descriptive analysis methods (e.g., Kaplan-Meier estimates, medians, confidence intervals) for the primary endpoint in Section 9.3.2.",
      "fix": "Add a detailed description of the descriptive analysis for PFS, including estimation methods and censoring rules."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing estimand attributes for PFS",
      "quote": "PFS, defined as the time from randomization date to the first documented PD, as assessed by investigator according to RECIST v1.1 or death due to any cause, whichever occurs first",
      "page": 35,
      "section": "Table 4",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The estimand for PFS lacks explicit specification of the intercurrent events (e.g., treatment switching, discontinuation) and the summary measure (e.g., hazard ratio, median difference).",
      "fix": "Define the estimand attributes for PFS, including handling of intercurrent events and the target summary measure."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing analysis for ORR endpoint",
      "quote": "ORR, defined as the proportion of participants with a CR or a PR on two consecutive occasions ≥4 weeks apart, as assessed by investigator according to RECIST v1.1",
      "page": 35,
      "section": "Table 4",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The statistical analysis section does not provide a specific analysis for ORR; it only gives general methods for categorical endpoints, but no explicit ORR analysis is described.",
      "fix": "Add a subsection for ORR analysis detailing the estimation, confidence intervals, and handling of missing responses."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing analysis for CBR and DCR endpoints",
      "quote": "CBR, defined as the proportion of participants who experience a best response of SD with a minimum duration of 6 months, a CR, or a PR, as assessed by investigator according to RECIST v1.1",
      "page": 35,
      "section": "Table 4",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "CBR and DCR are listed as endpoints but no specific statistical analysis is described for them in Section 9.3.",
      "fix": "Include analysis methods for CBR and DCR, including definitions of evaluable population and handling of missing data."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing analysis for safety endpoints",
      "quote": "Incidence and severity of adverse events, with severity determined according to the NCI CTCAE v5.0",
      "page": 35,
      "section": "Table 4",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The safety endpoints (AEs, ECOG, vital signs, labs) are listed but no detailed statistical analysis methods are provided in Section 9.3.",
      "fix": "Add a safety analysis subsection describing how each safety endpoint will be summarized and compared."
    },
    {
      "title": "Missing handling of missing data",
      "quote": "If a missing category is not presented in the data display, only patients with non-missing values for the parameter being assessed will be included in the percentage calculation.",
      "page": 82,
      "section": "9.3.1",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The protocol only mentions handling of missing categories in displays, but does not address missing data for primary or secondary endpoints (e.g., missing tumor assessments, missing lab values).",
      "fix": "Specify the methods for handling missing data for each endpoint, including sensitivity analyses."
    },
    {
      "title": "Sample size inputs missing",
      "quote": "Originally, the sample size of this study was determined by the primary endpoint; therefore, the study was event driven.",
      "page": 81,
      "section": "9.2",
      "category": "completeness",
      "severity": "major",
      "explanation": "The sample size section does not provide the original assumptions (e.g., expected PFS hazard ratio, event rates, alpha, power) used for the sample size calculation.",
      "fix": "Include the original sample size assumptions and calculation details, even if the study is now descriptive."
    },
    {
      "title": "Inconsistency in analysis sets for safety",
      "quote": "For safety analyses for the main treatment period, patients will be grouped according to whether any amount of experimental treatment is received, including cases in which experimental treatment was received in error.",
      "page": 82,
      "section": "9.2.1",
      "category": "consistency",
      "severity": "minor",
      "explanation": "The safety analysis set definition groups patients by experimental treatment received, but the table defines Safety as 'All patients who receive any amount of any study drug' which may include control drug; this could be inconsistent.",
      "fix": "Clarify whether the safety set includes patients who received only control treatment, and align the text with the table."
    }
  ]
}
